items.note: A store or building's information counter for directions and questions; contrast うけつけ (uketsuke) from an earlier lesson, the more general word for a reception desk in offices or hospitals.
Precedes a floor counter to specify a level below ground, e.g. ちか１かい (chika ikkai), 'basement 1st floor' — see that card.

その (sono) modifies a following noun ('that ___'); unlike それ (sore) from an earlier lesson, which stands alone as a pronoun ('that one'), その can't be used by itself. Compare この (kono) and あの (ano) for the same pronoun-vs-determiner pattern with これ (kore) and あれ (are).
Counter ほん (hon)/ぼん (bon)/ぽん (pon) for long, slender objects like bottles. Watch this one by ear: にほん (ni-hon) here is 'two long objects', identical in sound to にほん (nihon, 'Japan') from Lesson 1.
Counter まい (mai) for thin, flat objects.

items.target: レストランは５かいです
items.reading: レストランはごかいです

items.note: この (kono) modifies a following noun ('this ___'); unlike これ (kore) from an earlier lesson, which stands alone as a pronoun ('this one'), この can't be used by itself. Compare その (sono) and あの (ano) for the same pattern with それ (sore) and あれ (are).

items.target: このTシャツは2,000えんです
items.reading: このTシャツはにせんえんです

items.note: あの (ano) modifies a following noun ('that ___ over there'); unlike あれ (are) from an earlier lesson, which stands alone as a pronoun ('that one over there'), あの can't be used by itself. Compare この (kono) and その (sono) for the same pattern with これ (kore) and それ (sore).
A regular い-adjective placed directly before its noun, e.g. あおいTシャツ (aoi tii-shatsu); unlike あか (aka) or しろ (shiro), あお never drops its い to form a special wine compound — there's no あおワイン.

items.english: That blue T-shirt over there is 3,000 yen.
items.target: あのあおいTシャツは3,000えんです
items.reading: あのあおいTシャツはさんぜんえんです

items.note: Suffix — attaches after a number (written 〜まい (mai)).

Base reading of the long-object counter — after に (ni) (2), よん (yon) (4), ご (go) (5), なな (nana) (7), きゅう (kyuu) (9). Same sound and spelling as ほん (hon, 'Book') from Lesson 2 — two unrelated words that happen to share a form.
Voiced (dakuten) form of the long-object counter — after さん (san) (3), e.g. さんぼん (sanbon).
Plosive (handakuten) form — after いっ (ip) (1), ろっ (rop) (6), はっ (hap) (8), じゅっ (jup) (10), e.g. いっぽん (ippon).

Suffix — the general-purpose counter, used when no specific counter fits. Attaches to the native-Japanese numerals (ひと〜 (hito), ふた〜 (futa), みっ〜 (mit) → ひとつ (hitotsu), ふたつ (futatsu), みっつ (mittsu)). Written 〜つ (tsu).

items.note: Base adjective form; compare あかワイン (aka wain) (red wine), which is NOT あかい ワイン (akai wain) — see that card for the exception.
くろい (kuroi) is a regular い-adjective placed before its noun, e.g. くろいくつ (kuroi kutsu, 'black shoes'). Unlike あか (aka) and しろ (shiro), くろ has no special wine compound — there's no くろワイン.
Like あか (aka) in あかワイン (akawain, 'red wine'), しろ drops its い before ワイン: しろワイン (shirowain), 'white wine' — but keeps the full しろい form as a regular adjective before any other noun.

items.reviewNote: Shown in plain parentheses (not the wave-dash 〜 convention) rather than as a separate sub-entry.
items.note: お (o) is an optional polite prefix.
コップ (koppu) is the general word for a drinking glass or cup; contrast マグカップ (magukappu), a mug specifically, and コーヒーカップ (koohii kappu), a coffee cup typically served with a saucer.
Base reading of the floor counter — after most numbers (1 いっ (ik), 2 に (ni), 4 よん (yon), 5 ご (go), 6 ろっ (rok) …), e.g. ごかい (gokai) (5th floor).
Voiced (dakuten) form of the floor counter — after さん (san) (3), e.g. さんがい (sangai) (3rd floor).
Uses the voiced がい (gai) form after さん (san) — さんがい (sangai) — rather than the plain かい (kai) counter used after most other numbers.
Specifically a mug (from English 'mug cup'); contrast the more general コップ (koppu, glass/cup) and コーヒーカップ (kōhīkappu), a coffee cup typically served with a saucer.
A mikan is a satsuma / Japanese mandarin — a small, sweet, seedless, easy-to-peel citrus, extremely popular in Japan and a winter staple.

Fixed compound noun, NOT あかい ワイン (akai wain). Contrast the regular い-adjective+noun pattern, which keeps the い: あかい シャツ (akai shatsu) (“red shirt”), あおい Tシャツ (aoi T-shatsu) (“blue T-shirt”). Only these set colour-compounds drop it: あかワイン (aka wain) (“red wine”), しろワイン (shiro wain) (“white wine”).

items.note: Carries the honorific お (o) prefix seen earlier on おくに (okuni, 'your country'); おてあらい (otearai, literally 'hand-washing place') is the standard polite way to say restroom/toilet.
